source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Polynomial division over a field
statement: For f,g in F[x] with g nonzero, there are unique q,r in F[x] such that f=qg+r and either r=0 or deg(r)<deg(g).
conditions: F is a field.
g is nonzero.
conclusion: Division with remainder is valid and unique in F[x].
typical_uses: Reduce polynomial identities and prove ideal membership.
common_misuses: Using this division algorithm over a coefficient ring that is not a field.
bridge_lemmas: The leading coefficient of g is invertible in F.
repair_templates: Restrict coefficients to a field or use pseudo-division over a domain.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Gauss lemma and polynomial UFD transfer
statement: For a UFD R, the product of primitive polynomials is primitive; irreducibility over the fraction field is equivalent to irreducibility for primitive polynomials in R[x]. Consequently R[x] is a UFD.
conditions: R is a UFD.
Polynomials are primitive when irreducibility is transferred.
conclusion: Factorization in R[x] and Frac(R)[x] is controlled by contents and primitive parts.
typical_uses: Prove irreducibility over integers from irreducibility over rationals.
common_misuses: Ignoring polynomial content or assuming every irreducible over Frac(R) is primitive in R[x].
bridge_lemmas: content(fg)=content(f)content(g) up to a unit.
repair_templates: Separate content factors before applying the field criterion.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Hilbert basis theorem
statement: If R is Noetherian, then R[x] is Noetherian; iterating gives that every finitely generated polynomial ring over R is Noetherian.
conditions: R satisfies ACC on ideals.
conclusion: Every ideal in R[x_1,...,x_n] is finitely generated.
typical_uses: Justify termination of ideal and Grobner-basis arguments.
common_misuses: Applying it to infinitely generated polynomial rings without a finite-variable argument.
bridge_lemmas: Use leading-coefficient induction on an ascending chain of ideals.
repair_templates: State the finite number of variables and the Noetherian hypothesis explicitly.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Grobner remainder membership test
statement: For a Grobner basis G of an ideal I, multivariate division gives a unique remainder; a polynomial f lies in I exactly when its remainder on division by G is zero.
conditions: G is a Grobner basis for I under a fixed monomial order.
conclusion: Ideal membership is decidable by reduction to zero remainder.
typical_uses: Check polynomial consequences and construct explicit certificates.
common_misuses: Using an arbitrary generating set as if it were a Grobner basis.
bridge_lemmas: All S-polynomials reduce to zero for a Grobner basis.
repair_templates: Compute or certify a Grobner basis before invoking the remainder test.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Buchberger criterion
statement: A finite generating set G is a Grobner basis iff every pairwise S-polynomial reduces to zero modulo G.
conditions: A fixed monomial ordering is used.
Leading terms and S-polynomials are computed correctly.
conclusion: Vanishing S-polynomial remainders certify the Grobner basis property.
typical_uses: Repair incomplete ideal computations by adding nonzero S-polynomial remainders.
common_misuses: Checking only some pairs or using inconsistent leading-term orders.
bridge_lemmas: The leading-term ideal of G equals the ideal generated by all leading terms in I.
repair_templates: List every critical pair and reduce each S-polynomial to zero.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Tensor product universal property
statement: A bilinear map M x N -> P factors uniquely through a linear map M tensor_R N -> P sending m tensor n to the bilinear value.
conditions: M,N,P are R-modules and the map is R-bilinear.
conclusion: Tensor products represent bilinear maps and determine unique induced homomorphisms.
typical_uses: Construct maps out of tensor products and prove identities by checking pure tensors.
common_misuses: Treating tensors as ordered pairs or assuming every tensor has a unique pure-tensor form.
bridge_lemmas: Pure tensors generate M tensor_R N as an R-module.
repair_templates: Define the candidate map on pure tensors and verify bilinearity first.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Flatness and tensor exactness
statement: An R-module M is flat iff tensoring with M preserves injectivity of every map (equivalently, preserves every short exact sequence).
conditions: M is an R-module.
conclusion: Flatness is exactly exactness of the tensor functor - tensor_R M.
typical_uses: Detect when tensoring a proof preserves kernels and relations.
common_misuses: Assuming tensoring is always left exact.
bridge_lemmas: Tensor products are always right exact.
repair_templates: Add flatness or a field/PID hypothesis before preserving injections.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Rational canonical form
statement: Every linear transformation over a field is similar to a unique block diagonal matrix of companion matrices whose monic invariant factors satisfy a1|a2|...|am.
conditions: V is finite-dimensional over a field F.
conclusion: Invariant factors classify similarity over F and determine the minimal and characteristic polynomials.
typical_uses: Classify matrices without assuming eigenvalues lie in F.
common_misuses: Confusing rational canonical form with Jordan form or dropping the divisibility ordering.
bridge_lemmas: View V as a torsion F[x]-module with x acting as T.
repair_templates: Compute invariant factors via Smith form of xI-A.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Jordan diagonalizability criterion
statement: Over a field containing the eigenvalues, a linear map is diagonalizable iff its minimal polynomial splits into distinct linear factors (equivalently every Jordan block has size one).
conditions: The characteristic polynomial splits over the field.
conclusion: Absence of repeated factors in the minimal polynomial is equivalent to diagonalizability.
typical_uses: Diagnose claims that an eigenbasis exists.
common_misuses: Checking only the characteristic polynomial or ignoring field splitting.
bridge_lemmas: The minimal polynomial divides the characteristic polynomial.
repair_templates: Compute the minimal polynomial or eigenspace dimensions before asserting diagonalization.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Existence and uniqueness of splitting fields
statement: Every nonconstant polynomial over a field has a splitting field, and any two splitting fields are isomorphic by an isomorphism fixing the base field.
conditions: f is a polynomial over F.
conclusion: The splitting field is well-defined up to F-isomorphism.
typical_uses: Compare constructions of algebraic extensions and Galois groups.
common_misuses: Claiming literal equality of splitting fields rather than an F-isomorphism.
bridge_lemmas: Extend an isomorphism after adjoining one root, then induct on degree.
repair_templates: Replace equality by an isomorphism fixing F.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Splitting-field degree bound
statement: A splitting field of a degree-n polynomial over F has extension degree at most n! over F.
conditions: f has degree n over F.
conclusion: [K:F] <= n! for a splitting field K.
typical_uses: Bound Galois-group order and finite extension computations.
common_misuses: Assuming the bound is always attained.
bridge_lemmas: Adjoin roots one at a time; successive degrees are at most n,n-1,...,1.
repair_templates: Use the actual factorization to sharpen the bound when possible.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Fundamental theorem of Galois theory
statement: For a finite Galois extension K/F with group G, intermediate fields E correspond inclusion-reversingly to subgroups H: E=K^H and H=Gal(K/E). Degrees satisfy [K:E]=|H| and [E:F]=[G:H].
conditions: K/F is finite and Galois.
conclusion: Normal intermediate fields correspond exactly to normal subgroups and Gal(E/F) is G/H when H is normal.
typical_uses: Translate field lattice questions into subgroup calculations.
common_misuses: Applying the bijection to non-Galois or infinite extensions without modifications.
bridge_lemmas: The fixed field of a finite subgroup has degree equal to the subgroup order.
repair_templates: Verify finiteness and Galois hypotheses before invoking correspondence.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Linear independence of distinct characters
statement: Distinct multiplicative characters of a group with values in a field are linearly independent as functions.
conditions: Characters are distinct homomorphisms G -> L^x.
conclusion: No nontrivial L-linear relation among the characters exists.
typical_uses: Prove independence of field embeddings and bound automorphism groups.
common_misuses: Confusing character equality on generators with equality as functions.
bridge_lemmas: Choose an element where two characters differ and reduce the support of a dependence.
repair_templates: Use a minimal-support relation and translate it by a separating group element.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Cyclotomic extension degree
statement: The cyclotomic field Q(zeta_n) has degree phi(n) over Q and Gal(Q(zeta_n)/Q) is isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^x.
conditions: zeta_n is a primitive nth root of unity.
conclusion: Automorphisms are zeta_n -> zeta_n^a for a coprime to n.
typical_uses: Compute abelian Galois groups and construct subfields.
common_misuses: Using all residue classes a, including nonunits.
bridge_lemmas: The nth cyclotomic polynomial is the minimal polynomial of zeta_n over Q.
repair_templates: Restrict exponents to units modulo n and verify phi(n).

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Discriminant and alternating subgroup
statement: For a separable degree-n polynomial over F of characteristic not two, its Galois group is contained in A_n iff the discriminant is a square in F.
conditions: The polynomial is separable.
char(F) != 2.
conclusion: Square discriminant detects even permutations in the Galois group.
typical_uses: Narrow possible Galois groups of low-degree polynomials.
common_misuses: Using the test for inseparable polynomials or characteristic two.
bridge_lemmas: The square root of the discriminant changes sign under odd permutations.
repair_templates: Check separability and characteristic before using the discriminant criterion.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Hilbert theorem 90
statement: For a finite Galois extension K/F, every multiplicative 1-cocycle of Gal(K/F) in K^x is a coboundary; equivalently H^1(Gal(K/F),K^x)=0.
conditions: K/F is finite Galois.
conclusion: A cocycle a_sigma satisfies a_sigma=b^{-1}sigma(b) for some b in K^x.
typical_uses: Recognize norm-one elements and repair cyclic-extension arguments.
common_misuses: Applying the statement to arbitrary non-Galois extensions or additive modules.
bridge_lemmas: Use linear independence of automorphisms to choose b with nonzero cocycle sum.
repair_templates: State the Galois group action and cocycle convention explicitly.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Maschke theorem
statement: If G is finite and char(F) does not divide |G|, every FG-submodule has an FG-invariant complement; hence every finite-dimensional representation is completely reducible.
conditions: G is finite.
char(F) does not divide |G|.
conclusion: FG-modules split as direct sums of irreducibles.
typical_uses: Decompose representations and justify averaging projections.
common_misuses: Averaging by |G|^{-1} when the characteristic divides |G|.
bridge_lemmas: Average an arbitrary linear projection over the group.
repair_templates: Add the nondivisibility hypothesis or provide a separate modular argument.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Schur lemma
statement: A nonzero homomorphism between simple modules is an isomorphism; the endomorphism ring of a simple module is a division ring. Over an algebraically closed field, an irreducible finite-dimensional representation has only scalar commuting endomorphisms.
conditions: Modules are simple for the relevant ring.
conclusion: Intertwiners are invertible or zero, and central operators act as scalars over an algebraically closed field.
typical_uses: Prove irreducibility, uniqueness, and scalarity of commuting matrices.
common_misuses: Assuming scalarity over a non-algebraically closed field.
bridge_lemmas: Kernel and image of a module map are submodules.
repair_templates: Use the division-ring conclusion unless algebraic closure is explicitly available.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Character orthogonality relations
statement: For a finite group, irreducible complex characters are orthonormal under (chi,psi)=|G|^{-1} sum_g chi(g) conjugate(psi(g)); the number of irreducible characters equals the number of conjugacy classes.
conditions: G is finite and characters are complex irreducible characters.
conclusion: Inner products detect equality and irreducibility, and character tables have orthogonal rows and columns.
typical_uses: Decompose permutation characters and verify proposed character tables.
common_misuses: Forgetting conjugation or class-size weights.
bridge_lemmas: Characters are constant on conjugacy classes.
repair_templates: Rewrite sums over conjugacy classes with their sizes.

source: Dummit and Foote, Abstract Algebra.pdf; rewritten seed rule
name: Burnside p^a q^b theorem
statement: Every finite group whose order has at most two distinct prime divisors is solvable.
conditions: |G|=p^a q^b for primes p,q.
conclusion: G has a finite derived series ending in the identity.
typical_uses: Close solvability proofs after reducing group order.
common_misuses: Applying it to orders with three or more prime divisors.
bridge_lemmas: A nonabelian simple group cannot have a nonidentity conjugacy class of prime-power size.
repair_templates: Verify the group order has only two prime factors before invoking the theorem.
